comment: Ada versions (docs/specs/ada-cloud.md, 12): newest first. Each name maps to one release of ada-private's kernel (its CHANGELOG.md); `commit` is what the image installs (the latest stable's from uv.lock into the venv, every other one into /opt/ada/<kernel> by the Dockerfile). Dates are UTC days: deprecated from `deprecated`, retired from `ends`.

versions.name: ada-1-2-beta
versions.summary: Time can weigh: a model whose answers drift gives its newer precedents more say. Typed outputs and unions.
versions.notes:
When a model calibrates, ada-1-2-beta also tries giving each precedent less say as it ages, halving it every so often (its half-life), each held-out case asked at its own time. It keeps a half-life only when it clearly beats none on the model's newest precedents, so a model whose answers do not change over time reads exactly as before. A case is asked at its own time when the spec names one (`temporal_source`), else now. The setting `recency` turns it off.

A new setting, `level_weights`, is off by default: set to `roles`, a segment weighs as much as its roles' weights added up, so a segment of roles that tell nothing goes quiet. On German Credit it decided worse, so backtest it on your own model before you turn it on.

It includes ada-1-1-beta's change (a pair of values the model never learned stays out of the vote). Nothing stored changes, so moving to it and back is safe.

**Who it changes:** only models whose graded cases span at least a day and whose answers drift with time. German Credit and Banking77 give every answer exactly as on ada-1-1-beta (neither has time in it). Backtest your own model against it before you upgrade.

**Typed outputs (since 2026-10-28).** A named output can say what its answer is with `kind`: `choice` (the default), `score` (ordered levels: a mistake costs how many levels it is off, and an answer says the expected `level`), `noul` (yes or no, recorded as true or false, and an answer says `p`, the chance of yes), `number` (`number: {min, max, step}`, recorded as a number, and an answer says the expected `value`) or `many` (any of its values at once, recorded as a list). `when: {output, in}` makes an output one branch of a discriminated union: it is asked only when another output's answer is one of those values; a decide of every output answers a branch not taken with `applies: false`, and a case may not grade a branch its own answers leave out. A spec that uses none of these answers exactly as before.

- A beta: chosen only by name, never the default.
- Kernel 3.15.0 (3.14.0 until 2026-10-28; 3.15.0 changes no answer of a spec 3.14.0 reads).

versions.name: ada-1-1-beta
versions.summary: Learned pairs of roles stay out of a vote when the query's pair is one the model never learned.
versions.notes:
When a model learns that two roles tell more together than apart (a pair, such as how long a loan runs and how much is saved), it weighs each combination of their values it has learned from. Until now, a query bringing a combination the model had never learned from still gave that pair its full weight, and since the combination matched nothing stored, the pair pulled the vote toward no one in particular.

In ada-1-1-beta such a pair weighs nothing for that query, so the two roles' own weights decide, as they would in a model that had learned no pair. Nothing stored changes, so moving to it and back is safe.

**Who it changes:** only models that learned pairs (`interactions`, on by default), and only queries whose pair of values is new to the model. On German Credit it is within noise of ada-1-0 (deciding with costs: 70.5% right at a cost of 99, against 70.0% at 100). Backtest your own model against it before you upgrade.

- A beta: chosen only by name, never the default.
- Kernel 3.13.0.

versions.name: ada-1-0
versions.notes:
The version Ada Cloud launched with: typed answers with calibrated probabilities, the expected cost of each choice, asking a person when the spec prices it or the confidence is under its bar, and the precedents behind every answer. Models learn their roles', values', words' and pairs' weights from their own precedents, and big models are read through a shortlist and re-ranked exactly.

- Kernel 3.12.2.
